clue.text: I glance around like divine messenger

indicators.note: letters moved around are scattered out of their printed order and set down afresh

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone casts a glance about the room with the air of a heavenly herald.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words supply all seven letters; 'around' looks like part of the glancing but is the signal to rearrange them into ANGELIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is literally a messenger of God, so anything angelic resembles such a heavenly envoy.

clue.text: Heard flood survivor's development of story

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: Noah's ark survived the Biblical flood

explanation.surface: Someone hears how a tale about a survivor of a great flood unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessel that rode out the flood is the ark; said out loud it is identical to the spelling the definition wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative arc is the shape a plot follows from setup through climax to resolution in fiction.

clue.text: Sugar from Greek island used in gum

indicators.note: something used in a mixture is placed inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: gum is an adhesive, a kind of glue
Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A sweetener made from produce of a Greek island is added to chewing gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gum' reads as chewing gum but is the adhesive sense; the island goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, the main one carried in the blood and a common ingredient in sweets.

clue.text: Really enjoy being ahead in circuit race?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to relish eagerly, as a cat drinks cream
second meaning, read whimsically: one whole circuit ahead of rivals

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a runner who is a lap up has gone one full circuit further than the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is an idiom for accepting or enjoying it with great eagerness and delight.

clue.text: Options of frozen desserts with the fourth picked out

indicators.note: picking out one item removes it, and the ordinal says which letter position goes

parts.note: choc ices are ice-cream bars coated in chocolate, a British treat

explanation.surface: A menu offers a range of frozen desserts, one of which has been picked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Choc ices, the chocolate-coated ice-cream bars, lose their fourth letter, the second C.
explanation.definitionFit: Options and choices are near synonyms, both meaning the alternatives available to select between.

clue.text: Characters involved in kendo joined training facility

indicators.note: letters involved in a phrase are part of it, so the answer is a run of them

parts.note: the letters run across the word break

explanation.surface: Fighters who took up kendo signed up at a martial-arts gym.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'kendo' and the start of 'joined', fittingly, since kendo is practised in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is the hall or school where Japanese martial arts such as judo and karate are practised.

clue.text: Editor backed rival author

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
a rival or opponent is a foe

explanation.surface: A publisher's editor gave support to a competing novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' seems to mean supported, but it turns the editor round.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English writer of Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders, so he is a famous novelist.

clue.text: Cheese left in pots on ice

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first
one thing in another is enclosed by it, so a letter goes inside a word

parts.note: pots and jars are both containers
L is the abbreviation for left
a berg is a mass of floating ice

explanation.surface: Leftover cheese is kept in pots chilled on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for left slips inside the pots, and the ice chunk follows below.
explanation.definitionFit: Jarlsberg is a mild Norwegian cheese with large holes, similar in style to Swiss Emmental.

clue.text: Steal fruit from rugby players quietly

parts.note: the scrum is the pack of forwards bound together in rugby
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off with fruit taken quietly from a rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrumping is a British word for raiding orchards, especially by children stealing apples.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrump is British slang specifically for pilfering apples or other fruit from an orchard.

clue.text: In old make of car, cross English city

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it, so one letter is surrounded

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Ford is a car manufacturer
a cross is written as an X

explanation.surface: Driving a vintage motor, someone crosses an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross sits inside old plus the car make; 'cross' looks like a verb but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is the English university city on the Thames, the county town of Oxfordshire.

clue.text: Sharp-billed birds spooked crew at sea

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's crew out on the ocean is frightened by birds with pointed beaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooked' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'at sea' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodpeckers use their strong, chisel-like beaks to drill into tree bark for insects and nest holes.

clue.text: Recalled comic sketch set in outskirts of Hamilton

parts.note: a wit is a funny person, a comedian

indicators.note: something set in a frame is placed inside it, so one piece is enclosed
the outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the city name
to sketch is to draw

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch staged on the edge of Hamilton, Ontario, is remembered fondly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic sketch' reads as one phrase, but it splits into the funny person and the verb for drawing. 'Recalled' means taken back, as with a product, not remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: A product that has been recalled is withdrawn from sale, both meaning taken back or removed from circulation.

clue.text: Children of similar ability play on internet-enabled device

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a school class grouped by aptitude
second meaning: to watch or listen to media delivered over the web

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools pupils are streamed, sorted into sets by ability, so a top stream is a group of able children.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaming means playing video or music live over a network connection; a stream is also a school ability band.

clue.text: Crazy about an elevated lady in artwork

parts.note: crazy means mad
on can mean about, concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about a painting of a noblewoman raised up on high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated lady' suggests nobility, but 'elevated' only turns the two-letter word upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is the name for paintings and statues of the Virgin Mary, a constant subject of Western religious art.

clue.text: Tot and this writer start to relish hot weather?

parts.note: to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum
the setter refers to themself

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: A toddler and the writer both enjoy the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is an addition; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is the warmest season of the year, so it stands for a spell of hot weather.

clue.text: Wet items on ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, as coffee is, so the letters are broken and remixed

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Things lying on the floor are soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the floor, but here it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To wet something and to moisten it are synonyms, both meaning to make it damp with water.

clue.text: Ringing home good following argument

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the pieces before this word are placed later

parts.note: a ding-dong is British slang for a heated row
to be in is to be at home
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A phone rings at home just after a good quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A ding-dong is everyday British slang for a fierce argument; the home and good pieces come after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ding-donging imitates the repeated two-note chime of bells, so it describes something ringing out.

clue.text: Tender calves running uphill to some extent

indicators.note: in a down clue going uphill means reading from the bottom upwards
something true to some extent is only partly so, so only part of the phrase is used

parts.note: a run of letters across the word break

explanation.surface: Young cattle with sore legs struggle as they run up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective, sore, but it is a noun: one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is someone who looks after others, and a nurse is a carer who tends the sick.

clue.text: Identified fellow climbing English peak in danger

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a fellow is a man
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: the peak is the top, which in a down entry is the first letter of a word

parts.note: the first letter, its top in this down entry

explanation.surface: A climber on a perilous English mountain has been recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English peak' looks like a mountain, but English is just its abbreviation and 'peak in' picks the top letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone is to identify them, as when a suspect or witness is named in a report.

clue.text: Bleak nobleman in conversation

indicators.note: words in conversation are spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage

explanation.surface: A gloomy aristocrat holds forth while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: The titled lord's rank, said out loud, matches the adjective for desolate land.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak and barren both describe a landscape that is bare, desolate and lifeless.

clue.text: You are entering end of chess game fully developed

indicators.note: whatever enters something goes inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: checkmate ends a chess game
text-speak shorthand

explanation.surface: A player reaches the final stage of a game of chess, fully grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' suggests the last letter, but the whole chess finish is meant; 'you are' is the text-message U R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mature has reached its complete adult or ripened state, grown to full development.

clue.text: Regularly avoided greasy fish

indicators.note: avoiding something at regular intervals skips every other letter, leaving alternate ones

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone routinely steers clear of oily fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first, third and fifth letters and the even ones remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a flat cartilaginous sea fish with wing-like fins, related to sharks and skates.

clue.text: Formerly working, empty chute

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: emptying a word takes out its inside, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A chute that used to work now stands empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like an adjective on the chute, but it hollows the word out.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in the sense of at one time, previously, means the same as formerly.

clue.text: Fervour dancer represented with ultimate in energy

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

indicators.note: the ultimate is the very last, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter

explanation.surface: A performer portrayed dancing with great passion and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' looks like part of the theme but supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardency is the noun from ardent, meaning passionate zeal, so it is a synonym of fervour.
